claim: There exists a causal binary step-transition setting in which EMA lowers standard fixed-bin global ECE without lowering accuracy, while increasing discrete transition delay.
analytical_requirements: derive EMA states s1 through s4
prove s1 < 0.5, s2 < 0.5, and s3 > 0.5 throughout the parameter box
prove the 15-bin confidence assignments remain fixed throughout the box
derive raw and smoothed 15-bin ECE formulas under those assignments
prove the lower bound of raw ECE exceeds the upper bound of smoothed ECE throughout the box
numerical_requirements: verify the center construction exactly using rational arithmetic
verify lower ECE at 10, 15, 20, and 30 bins
verify equal accuracy and delay 0 versus delay 1
enumerate a bounded grid inside the open box as a computational cross-check
scope_boundary: This is an existence counterexample and mechanism illustration, not a universal theorem that EMA always improves ECE or always worsens delay.
failure_action: If the exact construction or interval proof fails, retain only a labeled toy illustration and do not expand theoretical scope.
